subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should Telegram `channels.telegram.accounts.<account>.direct.<peer>.tools` remain a supported enforcement boundary for per-DM tool access?
rationale: The schema and types still accept the field, but changing enforcement or retiring it affects operator security expectations and existing configs.

options.title: Enforce direct policy
options.body: Treat the accepted config as supported and implement a DM-aware resolver that preserves account, wildcard, sender, and thread precedence with Telegram live proof.

options.title: Retire with diagnostics
options.body: If direct-level tool policy is not supported, remove or migrate the accepted surface and add doctor/docs warnings so operators do not rely on a false deny boundary.

options.title: Document sender-policy workaround
options.body: Keep `direct.*.tools` unresolved for now but document global/per-agent `tools.toolsBySender` as the supported DM restriction path.

recommendation.title: Enforce direct policy
recommendation.body: Treat the accepted config as supported and implement a DM-aware resolver that preserves account, wildcard, sender, and thread precedence with Telegram live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent scoped group-policy work and timeline routing make this the best available owner for the security-boundary choice.
